card: Guide
What is USFans? How buying from Spain works (2026)
Understand purchasing, warehouse arrival, QC photos, consolidation and shipping to Spain.
12 min

content.standfirst: USFans is a purchasing agent connecting international buyers with sellers on Chinese shopping platforms. For a buyer in Spain, the process has four distinct stages: choose a current listing, arrange the purchase, inspect the item at the warehouse, and prepare international shipping. Understanding those stages helps you distinguish a product price from the delivered cost and an estimated delivery time from a promise. This guide explains the decisions involved and the evidence to keep at each stage.

sections.heading: What USFans does as a purchasing agent
paragraphs: USFans acts as an intermediary for purchases from platforms such as Taobao, 1688 and Weidian. The original seller supplies the item. The agent helps arrange the purchase, receive it at a warehouse, provide visual evidence and prepare an international parcel. These are separate responsibilities. A listing in an index does not establish that its price, production version, size or availability remains unchanged when you pay.

This website is an independent discovery guide and does not process orders. It organises product links and explains useful checks. Open the destination listing, check the domain, confirm the exact variant and save a reference before deciding. The index cannot make commitments on behalf of the seller or agent.

sections.heading: Search with a specific product in mind
paragraphs: Start with the garment type, size, colour, material, budget and details that matter to you. A search for a grey sweatshirt is broad; a zip-up sweatshirt with published measurements and a heavier fabric gives you clearer comparison criteria. Use a spreadsheet or category page to create a shortlist, then inspect each listing.

Check the title, photographs, options, size chart, current price, estimated domestic delivery and any notices. Save the URL and selected variant. If several versions have unclear names, ask for a measurable distinction. A higher price alone does not establish better quality.

sections.heading: What happens after placing the order
paragraphs: After payment, the agent arranges the purchase with the seller. The order may move through stages such as awaiting purchase, ordered, dispatched by the seller and received at the warehouse. Labels can change, so read the current explanation in your account and follow the sequence instead of relying on terminology from an old tutorial.

The journey to the warehouse depends mainly on the seller and domestic transport within China. Keep this separate from international shipping to Spain. If the order stops progressing, check stock notices, messages and requests for additional payment before treating the delay as a transport problem.

sections.heading: Use QC photos to check visible details
paragraphs: When an item arrives, the warehouse inspection and QC photographs help you review its visible identity, colour, label size, quantity, general shape and obvious damage. They do not prove authenticity, internal composition, durability or a perfect fit. Compare the evidence with the variant you saved before ordering.

For clothing, inspect the front, back, print, fastenings, seams and labels. For footwear, compare both shoes, including toes, heels, sides, soles and size labels. If a missing detail would change your decision, request a specific photograph or measurement and check the current service conditions first.

sections.heading: Consolidation requires a packing decision
paragraphs: Consolidation groups accepted items into a parcel. It can reduce repeated charges, but a bulky, fragile or restricted item can increase chargeable weight or limit the shipping options for the entire parcel. Compare one parcel with two using current measurements and quotations. There is no ideal parcel weight for every destination.

Decide which packaging to keep, remove, compress or reinforce. Removing a box may reduce volume while reducing protection. A packing rehearsal can provide more realistic dimensions before the final payment. Include only accepted items and resolve open returns before consolidating them.

sections.heading: Choose an eligible service to Spain
paragraphs: Check eligibility before comparing prices. Consider actual and volumetric weight, total cost, tracking, estimated transit time, content limits, compensation and destination requirements. A cheap service is unsuitable if it excludes your contents or postcode. Mainland Spain, the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla must not be treated as one uniform delivery territory.

The delivered cost may include products, domestic transport, international shipping, currency conversion, selected services, taxes and customs handling. Spanish tax guidance describes a new fixed duty applying from July 2026 to certain distance purchases worth up to €150 from outside the EU. Check the current rule and identify charges already collected.

sections.heading: A practical sequence for your first purchase
paragraphs: Identify the product, open its current listing, save the variant and estimate the full cost before placing the order. At warehouse arrival, compare QC with your reference and resolve discrepancies. Then calculate the parcel using realistic measurements, select an available service for its contents and destination, verify the address and phone number, and retain the tracking number.

This sequence helps prevent late decisions. It cannot guarantee seller performance, acceptance of a return, a delivery date or customs treatment. It can help you avoid ordering the wrong variant, accepting a visible defect, mixing incompatible contents or paying for shipping before checking the full cost.

card: Clothing
USFans clothing: find current links and compare products
Check clothing links, measurements, variants and QC before adding items to a parcel.
11 min

content.standfirst: Searching for USFans clothing usually means finding current product links or deciding whether a particular garment is suitable. A useful guide helps with both. Shoes, sweatshirts, T-shirts, jackets and sports jerseys need different checks, but every choice should end at the current product listing. Old spreadsheets, vague titles and attractive photographs are not enough to establish which variant is available or whether it will fit.

sections.heading: Use a spreadsheet to discover current listings
paragraphs: A USFans spreadsheet collects links and speeds up discovery. Its date matters because sellers can change prices, remove sizes, replace photographs or close listings. Treat the index as a route to a verifiable product page. It does not prove stock or quality. If a link no longer opens the advertised option, find the current reference or remove it from your shortlist.

Keep a short list with the URL, category, variant, size, observed price and date checked. This makes similar products easier to compare. Hundreds of saved links are less useful if you never return to verify them.

sections.heading: Footwear: size, symmetry and parcel volume
paragraphs: The nominal shoe size is only a starting point. Look for a usable chart, inner length or insole measurement where available, and clear label photographs. Check whether the listing distinguishes production versions or batches. Compare foot measurements and the required allowance instead of relying only on an automatic EU, US or Chinese size conversion.

Shoe boxes occupy space and affect shipping. Decide whether their structural protection matters before removing them. In QC, inspect the whole pair: toes, heels, sides, soles and labels. One attractive photograph of a single shoe does not establish that the pair is symmetrical.

sections.heading: Sweatshirts and T-shirts: measure a reference garment
paragraphs: Measure the chest width, overall length, shoulders and sleeves of a similar garment that already fits. Compare with the seller’s chart and establish whether it describes the garment or the wearer’s body. S, M and XL do not represent consistent dimensions across manufacturers or different versions of a listing.

Check published composition, fabric weight only when a verifiable figure exists, cut and details such as the zip, hood, cuffs or print. In QC, inspect the size label, graphic position, main seams and obvious colour differences. Lighting changes the appearance of colours, so avoid firm conclusions based on one photograph.

sections.heading: Jackets: structure, filling and restrictions
paragraphs: A jacket may occupy more parcel space than its weight suggests. Check measurements with the garment fastened, sleeve length, hood, pockets and fastening system. If a listing mentions a material or filling without a verifiable specification, treat it as the seller’s description rather than certification.

Compression can reduce the volume of soft clothing, but it can also distort finishes and may be unsuitable for certain materials. Decide on packaging after seeing the item and the actual options for your shipping service. Advice for another parcel with different contents may not apply.

sections.heading: Sports jerseys: name, number and version
paragraphs: Distinguish the version, season, colour, size and any personalisation. Confirm whether a name or number belongs to the selected option or appears only in promotional photography. Personalised garments may have different return conditions, so document the selection before paying.

Check the front, back, badge, sponsors, name, number, collar and labels in QC. Ask for specific evidence if a measurement or print detail determines acceptance. Visual inspection can identify visible discrepancies; it does not prove authenticity.

sections.heading: Recognise a useful listing
paragraphs: A useful listing identifies the exact option, provides sufficient images, offers understandable measurements and displays relevant notices or conditions. A weak listing uses generic titles, combines unexplained versions or lacks size references. A low price does not solve uncertainty about the product you are selecting.

Open the destination before payment. Check the expected domain, matching product, current price and available options. Keep links that pass these checks and save enough information to compare the received item later.

sections.heading: A repeatable clothing purchase process
paragraphs: Filter by category, shortlist a few candidates, compare measurements and variants, estimate weight and volume, and record your selection. After warehouse arrival, inspect QC with a checklist appropriate to the garment. Decide whether to accept it, request more evidence, seek a return or include it in the parcel.

The aim is a verifiable purchase decision. A long list of product names is less useful than knowing the size, version and likely logistics cost of each item you order. Resolve those points before the garment reaches the warehouse whenever possible.

card: Reviews
USFans reviews and reliability: what to check before buying
Evaluate the agent, seller, QC evidence and shipping conditions using specific, verifiable information.
11 min

content.standfirst: A promotional sentence cannot settle searches for USFans reviews or whether USFans is reliable. Several separate questions matter: are you on the expected domain, is the advertised service available, has the seller supplied the correct item, does QC provide useful evidence, and is shipping suitable? Returns, transport restrictions and import obligations also affect the outcome. This method helps you investigate without treating one customer’s experience as a universal result.

sections.heading: Separate the agent, seller and carrier
paragraphs: USFans acts as an agent between buyers and sellers on Chinese platforms. The agent can arrange purchasing, receive goods and prepare parcels. The seller still influences stock, the selected variant, visible quality and delivery to the warehouse. International transport and final delivery involve further operators.

A review saying everything was perfect or everything went wrong may describe only one stage. Identify what happened, when, in which country, with what product and at which stage of the order. Without this context, the review has limited value for assessing your own situation.

sections.heading: Check the destination before entering information
paragraphs: Enter the expected domain directly or use a bookmark you have checked. Review the connection, account details and payment page before entering information. Be cautious about private messages asking you to leave the normal process, download unfamiliar files or transfer funds to a different account without a verifiable explanation.

This website is independent and links to an external product catalogue. It is not the official USFans platform. Read the notice and confirm each link’s destination. A similar design, logo or search position does not establish ownership.

sections.heading: Distinguish advertised services from guarantees
paragraphs: The official beginner guide describes purchasing, warehouse arrival, inspection, consolidation and shipping. Public product pages can show QC photographs and conditions for requesting returns. These establish which functions are advertised, but they do not guarantee the same outcome for every order.

Save the conditions visible when ordering: selected option, price, notices, applicable policy and services. If an important condition is not published or visible in your account, treat it as unconfirmed. Do not fill the gap with amounts or policies taken from old videos.

sections.heading: Read reviews with enough context
paragraphs: Look for recurring patterns across independent, recent sources. Separate comments about the interface, support, seller, QC, packaging, transport and customs. Compare countries and dates. A service available in another market may not be available in Spain, and a delay during a busy period does not establish a permanent delivery time.

Give more weight to a clear sequence, approximate dates and a documented result than to comments without details. Screenshots can help, but may omit context or be edited. Do not republish other people’s names, addresses, order references or tracking numbers.

sections.heading: Consider useful evidence and its limits together
paragraphs: Clear listings, recorded selections, understandable status changes, usable photographs and shipping conditions visible before payment are useful signs. Keeping your own records also makes it easier to ask support a precise question when something differs from the order.

None of these removes all risk. The agent does not manufacture the item, QC is visual, returns depend on the applicable conditions, transport has restrictions, and the destination may require taxes or formalities. A balanced assessment includes both the evidence and these limits.

sections.heading: Start with an order you can document
paragraphs: If you decide to try the service, consider a simple, well-described item at a cost you can accept. Avoid combining restricted, personalised or difficult-to-measure products in the first order. Document the listing, variant, payment, arrival, QC, packing instructions and tracking.

The first purchase cannot prove that every future order will have the same result. It can show whether you understand the process and can record each stage. Difficulty documenting or resolving a small issue is more useful information than an unsupported general rating.

sections.heading: Decide whether the process suits your needs
paragraphs: Confirm the domain, agent’s role, seller, option, measurements, probable cost, visible policy, QC limitations, available shipping service and import obligations. Decide how much uncertainty and waiting time you can accept. A fixed delivery deadline, certified authenticity or a straightforward local return may require a different purchasing arrangement.

Make the decision from current evidence and your requirements. An isolated positive or negative review should not replace checks on the actual listing, parcel and destination. Keep unresolved questions visible instead of treating missing information as reassurance.

card: Canary Islands
USFans shipping to the Canary Islands: checks before payment
Verify postcode eligibility, packing, documentation and Canary Islands import requirements.
10 min

content.standfirst: Shipping a USFans parcel to the Canary Islands needs its own checks. A price or service quoted for mainland Spain does not establish island coverage, the same delivery time or identical tax treatment. Start with the exact postcode and the actual parcel, then verify the available service and import requirements. This guide is a checklist for obtaining a usable quotation, not a promise that a particular route is currently available.

sections.heading: Confirm coverage for the exact postcode
paragraphs: Enter the complete destination and postcode when estimating or preparing the parcel. Check that the service accepts the Canary Islands rather than assuming that a general Spain label includes every territory. Availability can depend on contents, dimensions, weight and the current service rules.

If the account does not provide a suitable option, ask support about the specific destination and parcel. A screenshot from another date or a quote for mainland Spain does not confirm current eligibility. Do this before paying for international shipping.

sections.heading: Keep the island and address details consistent
paragraphs: Use the recipient’s name, street, building details, town, province or island as required, postcode and reachable telephone number. Check that the postcode corresponds to the actual delivery location and that the form retains all essential information.

If the address fields are unclear, request clarification. Do not change the postcode or select an inaccurate mainland destination to make a shipping option appear. An apparently accepted form does not establish that the carrier can deliver the parcel as addressed.

sections.heading: Check Canary Islands import requirements
paragraphs: The Canary Islands have a distinct indirect-tax framework, including IGIC. Mainland VAT assumptions and a mainland shipping price should not be copied into an island budget. Review current information from the Canary Islands tax authority and the carrier for your transaction and contents.

Establish which taxes, declarations and handling services are included in the quotation and which may be charged separately. Keep uncertainty explicit until you receive a clear breakdown. This guide does not assign one fixed import amount to every parcel.

sections.heading: Prepare the supporting documents
paragraphs: Keep the product descriptions, quantities, invoices or purchase records, payment evidence and shipping information. The customs process or carrier may request supporting documents. Their details should correspond to the actual goods and amounts paid.

Use accurate information and follow the procedure communicated for your parcel. If a request is unclear, verify it through the recognised account or carrier channel. Retain copies and avoid publishing personal documents or complete tracking details.

sections.heading: Calculate the packed parcel
paragraphs: Use realistic final weight and external dimensions, including packaging and protection. A lightweight but bulky parcel can have a higher chargeable weight. The sum of estimated product weights is not a substitute for the prepared parcel’s measurements.

Compare packaging options where they are available. Removing a box may save space but reduce protection. A packing rehearsal can help establish dimensions; confirm the service conditions and compare the resulting quote with the same contents and destination.

sections.heading: Compare eligible services on the same basis
paragraphs: Record total cost, chargeable weight, tracking, estimated time, restrictions, protection and known customs-related charges. Eliminate ineligible services first. Among the remaining options, compare cost and traceability together using consistent parcel information.

Do not treat an estimated date as an appointment. Processing, export, flights, customs and island delivery can all affect timing. If you need an item by a critical date, allow sufficient margin or reconsider the purchasing method.

sections.heading: Final checks before paying for shipping
paragraphs: Confirm that all items are accepted, open returns are resolved, the address retains the correct island and postcode, the phone number works, and the contents meet the service rules. Check that the quoted weight matches the prepared parcel and identify charges included or potentially payable at destination.

Pay only after resolving important uncertainties and save the conditions. Current account information establishes operational availability for the parcel. Official Canary Islands and Spanish sources provide the reference for the applicable import procedures and taxes.

card: Shipping services
Spanish Line Packet on USFans: how to compare the service
Check eligibility, chargeable weight, total cost, tracking and current conditions before choosing a route.
9 min

content.standfirst: Spanish Line Packet is a shipping-service name that users search for when comparing USFans delivery options. The name alone does not prove that it is available for every parcel or that it is the cheapest or fastest choice. Evaluate the current quotation for your account, destination and contents. Chargeable weight, tracking, restrictions, estimated time and compensation all matter alongside the price.

sections.heading: Confirm the currently available service
paragraphs: Commercial names can change or cover different services. Open the shipping estimate or parcel-creation page and check whether Spanish Line Packet appears for your exact postcode and contents. An old screenshot, a table for another country or a video recommendation is not confirmation.

Read the complete description, including weight range, dimensions, accepted contents, surcharges, tracking, estimated time and protection conditions. Ask for clarification before payment if material information is missing.

sections.heading: Calculate chargeable weight
paragraphs: Compare actual and volumetric weight according to the displayed rules. A light parcel with large dimensions may be charged at a much higher weight. Include the outer box, wrapping and protective materials. Adding estimated product weights rarely reproduces the final parcel exactly.

Soft clothing may allow compression, while footwear, bags or fragile items may need structural protection. Compare two packing scenarios when the difference matters and consider a packing rehearsal if that service is available.

sections.heading: Check contents and territory restrictions
paragraphs: Batteries, liquids, cosmetics, magnets, food and other sensitive contents can limit the available services. An attractive option for T-shirts may disappear after a restricted item is added. Review every item before consolidating the parcel.

Spain is not a uniform delivery territory. Confirm mainland Spain, the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Ceuta or Melilla using the exact postcode. The word Spanish in a service name does not establish coverage.

sections.heading: Compare the complete quotation
paragraphs: Record international transport, packing, selected services, conversion costs and potential destination charges. A lower base rate may offer poorer value if the service uses a higher chargeable weight or requires additional services. Allow for changes between estimated and final measurements.

Also check what happens if delivery fails, documents are requested or the parcel is returned. Compensation conditions, exclusions and required evidence can matter more than a small difference in the initial price.

sections.heading: Understand tracking and the estimated time
paragraphs: Check the tracking events provided and identify the final delivery operator where possible. There may be periods without updates between departure and the first local scan. A pause alone does not establish loss; compare it with the service’s published range and the parcel’s actual stage.

Save the parcel reference, tracking number, payment date and service conditions. If the stated support threshold is exceeded, send a specific enquiry with those details instead of several messages without a clear reference.

sections.heading: Check taxes and customs handling
paragraphs: A shipping-service name does not remove import obligations. Check whether the quotation explains taxes or customs procedures and compare it with current official Spanish guidance. From July 2026, a fixed duty applies to certain distance purchases worth up to €150 from outside the EU, alongside applicable VAT.

Do not describe a service as having no customs process unless its current conditions explain the arrangement precisely. Even when a charge is collected in advance, retain invoices and payment evidence.

sections.heading: Make a six-column comparison
paragraphs: Compare Spanish Line Packet with other available options using eligibility, chargeable weight, total cost, tracking, estimated time and protection. Exclude incompatible services. Choose among the remainder according to parcel value, urgency, clarity of conditions and the uncertainty you can accept.
Repeat the comparison immediately before payment because rates, capacity and rules can change. This guide provides a method; it does not confirm that the service is enabled for a particular parcel.

card: Tracking
USFans shipping times and tracking to Spain
Separate seller dispatch, warehouse processing, international transport and final delivery.
9 min

content.standfirst: USFans delivery to Spain is not one continuous countdown with a universal deadline. Seller dispatch, warehouse decisions, parcel preparation and international transport are separate stages. Customs and final delivery add further steps. Distinguishing them helps you understand tracking, identify where a pause occurs and ask a useful question without assuming that every period without a scan means a lost parcel.

sections.heading: Stage one: seller and domestic transport
paragraphs: After ordering, the agent arranges the purchase and the seller prepares and dispatches the item. Stock availability, preorders, personalisation and domestic transport all affect timing. This stage ends when the warehouse records receipt, rather than when you pay for the product.

If the status does not change, check stock notices, price differences and account messages. An order that has not reached the warehouse cannot be investigated through the international carrier’s tracking system.

sections.heading: Stage two: receipt, QC and your decision
paragraphs: The warehouse records the item and provides QC photographs. Time spent reviewing them, requesting a measurement or arranging a return contributes to the overall wait even though no international parcel exists yet. Review this stage promptly so that you do not miss a seller’s return window.

Give each item a clear decision: accept, ask for information, return or wait. Resolve open issues before consolidation. International tracking relates to the parcel created for dispatch; warehouse arrival alone does not mean that international transport has begun.

sections.heading: Stage three: parcel preparation and dispatch
paragraphs: After you select items, packaging and a shipping service, the warehouse prepares, measures and labels the parcel before handing it to the logistics network. A tracking number can be created before the first physical movement. Information received does not mean that a flight has departed.

Save the payment date, parcel reference, weight, service and packing instructions. A weight or contents review may require action in your account before dispatch. Check notifications before attributing the pause to the carrier.

sections.heading: Read tracking as a sequence of events
paragraphs: Group events into electronic information, collection, export, transport, arrival in the destination country, customs, local delivery and receipt. Automatic translations can vary. Focus on location, date and the transition between stages rather than one isolated word.

Different tracking systems may update at different times. Compare the agent’s tracking with the final carrier when available. Keep the full tracking number private because it can expose information about delivery.

sections.heading: Know when to contact support
paragraphs: Check the estimated service range and its stated support threshold. Holidays, busy periods, air capacity, inspections and transfers to a local operator can create gaps. A short pause within the estimate does not by itself establish a problem.

If the parcel exceeds the relevant threshold or shows an explicit exception, prepare an enquiry with the parcel reference, tracking number, last event, date and a screenshot without unnecessary private data. A precise description helps support identify the stage involved.

sections.heading: Customs and final delivery in Spain
paragraphs: Arrival in the destination country does not mean immediate delivery. Customs checks, document requests, payments or transfer to the local operator may follow. Keep the invoice, payment record and contents description available if requested.

After clearance, follow the local carrier’s tracking when available. Check the address, phone number, delivery attempts and any collection point. Procedures for the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla can differ from mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands.

sections.heading: Plan using ranges rather than promises
paragraphs: Allow separate time ranges for the seller, QC, your decisions, packing and transport, plus a margin for customs and local delivery. A purchase through an international chain may be unsuitable for an immovable deadline. Estimates describe possible timing and do not guarantee a delivery appointment.

The current order status and the service conditions applicable when you pay are your most relevant operational references. Keep a simple record and act when there is a specific exception or when the stated threshold is exceeded.

card: Returns
USFans warehouse returns: a practical checklist
Inspect QC promptly, document discrepancies and confirm conditions before requesting a return.
9 min

content.standfirst: A return from the USFans warehouse happens before international shipping. It depends on the seller, product type, item condition, evidence and terms shown for the order. Some public listings describe a request within five days of warehouse arrival followed by negotiation with the seller. That is not a promise of automatic acceptance or a free return. Check the policy and deadline applicable to your own order.

sections.heading: Read the conditions before purchasing
paragraphs: Before payment, look for notices about personalisation, hygiene, preorders, exchanges, returns and domestic shipping. Save the selected variant and important conditions. If the option is non-returnable or the policy is unclear, decide whether that uncertainty is acceptable before ordering.
Do not apply one seller’s conditions to another. Products purchased through the same agent can have different policies. The current listing and order details are the relevant references.

sections.heading: Inspect promptly when QC becomes available
paragraphs: Compare the product, colour, size, quantity, shape, visible damage, accessories and important details with your saved order. Enlarge the photographs. If the view needed to establish a problem is missing, request a specific photo or measurement and check the service cost.

A statement such as I do not like it is less specific than I ordered XL but the label shows M. Describe visible facts and identify the supporting order detail and photograph. This makes the discrepancy easier to verify.

sections.heading: Understand a stated five-day request period
paragraphs: Where a listing states that a return may be requested within five days after warehouse arrival, read it as a request window followed by the applicable seller process. Acceptance, method and charges still depend on the terms. Do not assume that the same window applies to every item.

Act promptly and use the deadline or countdown displayed for your order. Do not leave a necessary photo request until the last moment or add a disputed item to an international parcel. Once international dispatch is being processed, the available options can change.

sections.heading: Prepare a verifiable request
paragraphs: Include the order reference, requested variant, observed discrepancy, relevant QC photo and desired resolution. Keep the message concise and factual. For a measurement issue, identify the exact measuring points; for missing pieces, state the expected and received quantities.

Avoid contradictory requests or repeated messages that obscure the facts. Save the response, conditions, return cost and date. A clear record helps you evaluate whether to accept the item, exchange it or proceed with a return.

sections.heading: Confirm possible costs and outcomes
paragraphs: The seller may accept a return, offer an exchange, request evidence, impose conditions or decline. Domestic return shipping and other charges may apply. Do not treat a requested return as free or completed until the account confirms the amounts and outcome.

Compare the time and cost of returning with the item’s value and the consequences of keeping it. This comparison does not require you to accept an incorrect product. It helps clarify the available choices before you decide.

sections.heading: Keep disputed items out of consolidation
paragraphs: Leave the item out of the parcel while a question, return or exchange remains unresolved. Premature consolidation can add work or restrict options. Confirm that the final decision is reflected in the order before paying for international shipping.
If a replacement arrives, inspect its variant and QC as a new receipt. Do not assume that an exchange automatically resolves the original discrepancy.

sections.heading: Final return checklist
paragraphs: Check the saved policy, arrival date, visible deadline, selected variant, QC evidence, factual description, requested solution, charges and parcel status. Retain communications and avoid exposing personal information in public posts.

This guide cannot guarantee seller acceptance. Its purpose is to help you submit a clear request while the item is still in China and avoid losing options through missing evidence or premature consolidation.
